sources.venue: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering 447, 118358

Paper introduction and conclusion on thermodynamic scope and damage benchmark
sources.method_fact: Short observable strain-stress history plus next strain increment drives an attention/U-Net/Fourier autoregressive operator; teacher forcing is phased out.
limitations: Finite history window is not a general sufficient-statistic theorem
Rate-independent benchmarks do not establish rate-dependent viscoelastic transfer
Observed initial stress history is richer than unknown local stresses in robot contact
No blanket structural thermodynamic guarantee inferred from low trajectory error

sources.method_fact: Function-valued microstructure conditions recurrent ODE state and stress mappings; 1D Kelvin-Voigt homogenization supplies a uniform-approximation result.
limitations: Theory requires positive bounded material fields, bounded variation and bounded strain/rate classes
Main theorem concerns 1D linear viscoelasticity, not arbitrary finite-strain plasticity
Forward-Euler training and zero-state penalty are not structural discrete passivity
Microstructure is provided as input

sources.method_fact: Nonnegative nonlocal kernel and monotone learned bond response induce conditional energy convexity; training uses observed displacement/body-force pairs.

Vectorized autodiff is an implementation advance already present, not an empty novelty slot

sources.method_fact: Joint energy/yield/flow/hardening learning with a thermodynamic relation between flow potential and yield surface, plus implicit gradients and custom spectral Hessians.
limitations: Infinitesimal strain, rate-independent, isotropic plasticity
Known classical laws, synthetic specimen data and foam RVE in inspected evidence
Does not by itself establish finite-strain viscoelastic memory or online adaptation
Implicit differentiation assumes a suitable converged nonsingular local solution branch
